parameters.content:
## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n downloads the finished MP4 and renders it as
an inline video player with a download button — no URL to copy anywhere.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (and `jobId`,
`creditsCharged`) if you want to pipe the result onward.

## Daily quiz Shorts on autopilot

Every day this workflow reads the next unused question from your Google Sheet and
renders a 1080x1920 quiz Short with Zvid: **question + three options → an animated
3-2-1 countdown → the correct answer highlighted, with a fun fact**. After a real
render it writes the video URL back to the sheet so a row is never reused.

### Setup (about five minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*, *Submit render*
   and *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** — attach a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential to *Get quiz rows*
   and *Mark row done*, then pick your spreadsheet + tab in BOTH nodes.
   The expected columns are on the yellow note.
3. **Open `Config`** and set your brand name, handle and colours. Every knob
   lives there — nothing is buried in the nodes.
4. Run **Test manually**. With the shipped default (`dryRun: false`) this
   **renders for real and spends credits** — about **15 credits** per video
   (free accounts include enough to test).
   *Want a free look first?* Set `dryRun: true` in **Config** and the run stops
   at a free validate: exact credit price plus an **editorLink** that opens the
   draft in the Zvid editor. Nothing is charged and the sheet row stays unused.
5. Click **▶ Watch video** (the last node on the canvas) to play the finished
   MP4 right inside n8n.

The schedule fires daily; fill the sheet once a month and it works through it
row by row.

## Your quiz sheet

Header row (exact spelling, row 1):

`Question | OptionA | OptionB | OptionC | CorrectLetter | FunFact | Status | VideoUrl`

- **Question** — up to 130 characters. Long questions automatically get a
  smaller font and a little more reading time.
- **OptionA/B/C** — up to 40 characters each.
- **CorrectLetter** — `A`, `B` or `C`.
- **FunFact** — one sentence shown after the reveal (up to 200 characters).
- Leave **Status** and **VideoUrl** empty. The workflow takes the FIRST row with
  an empty Status; after a real render it writes `done` + the video URL there.
  Dry runs never touch the sheet.

Rows with anything in Status are skipped, so you can park a row by typing
`skip` into its Status cell.

## The three beats

1. **Question** — brand pill, the question, A/B/C option rows, handle watermark.
2. **Countdown** — full-screen 3 · 2 · 1 with rotating accent colours. Digits
   crossfade, so a paused frame never shows an empty ring.
3. **Reveal** — the correct row lights up with a check mark, wrong answers dim
   to 35%, and a "DID YOU KNOW?" card shows your FunFact.

Type sizes adapt to content length, and the layout is computed so nothing ever
overlaps — a 130-character question and 40-character options still fit. Every
element ends above the caption strip the Shorts player draws along the bottom
of the frame; the only things below the main content are the small handle
watermark and the brand line.

The music bed is HEAD-checked before use; if the URL is dead or over the plan's
audio size cap the video simply renders without music — a nice-to-have can
never fail the run.

## Dry run — the free preview (opt-in)

The workflow ships with `dryRun: false`, so a run renders for real and spends
credits. Set `dryRun: true` in **Config** to take this branch instead.

A dry run validates the payload against your real plan limits, quotes the exact
credit cost, and saves the project as a **draft**, then reports an
**editorLink** like

`https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the video, tweak wording or colours by hand, and check the
timing before you spend a single credit. The sheet row is NOT marked as used by
a dry run.

When the draft looks right, set `dryRun` back to `false` to render it.

## Posting to YouTube Shorts

The run ends with the MP4 URL written back to your sheet — post it manually or
bolt on a publish tail after *Run summary*:

1. **HTTP Request** — GET `{{ $json.videoUrl }}`, response format **File**.
   (This is exactly what *▶ Watch video* already does, so you can also just
   branch your upload node off that one.)
2. **YouTube** node (OAuth2) — operation *Upload*: title = the question,
   add `#Shorts` to the description, keep privacy `private` or `unlisted`
   until you have watched a few. A 9:16 video under 3 minutes is automatically
   a Short.

Swap the tail for TikTok, Instagram or Google Drive — everything before it
stays identical.

On self-hosted n8n you can also install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and replace *Submit render* + *Wait* + *Get render
status* with the native **Zvid** node and **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) —
that removes the polling loop entirely.
